faq.q: Does getting a filling hurt?
faq.a: If needed, local anaesthetic is used and you won't feel pain during the procedure. Very small, shallow cavities may not need anaesthetic.

faq.q: When can I eat after a filling?
faq.a: A white filling sets instantly. If you had anaesthetic, wait until the numbness wears off, usually 1–3 hours.

faq.q: Is sensitivity after a filling normal?
faq.a: Mild cold sensitivity for the first few days is normal. Come back for a check if pain lasts more than a week or wakes you at night.

faq.q: Can I have a filling while pregnant?
faq.a: Yes. Fillings are among the treatments that can be done safely in pregnancy; the second trimester is usually the best time.

faq.q: How many fillings can be done in one day?
faq.a: Depending on where the teeth are and how large the fillings are, several can be done in one session.

title: Scale and polish in Beylikdüzü: how often should you have it, and does it hurt?
desc: Scale and polish (professional teeth cleaning) in Beylikdüzü: how long it takes, whether it hurts or damages enamel, how often you need it, and sensitivity and gum bleeding afterwards. Dent32 Beylikdüzü.
seoTitle: Scale and polish in Beylikdüzü | Dent32
seoDesc: Scale and polish: how long it takes, whether it hurts or harms enamel, how often you need it, and sensitivity or bleeding afterwards.
lead: A scale and polish removes hardened plaque (tartar) from the teeth and along the gum line with ultrasonic instruments, then polishes the surface. It usually takes 30–45 minutes, doesn't damage enamel and is recommended every 6–12 months for most people. Tartar that a toothbrush can't remove is the most common cause of bleeding gums, bad breath and gum recession.

sections.html:
A layer of bacterial plaque forms on the teeth every day. Plaque that isn't removed by brushing and flossing hardens within a few days, combining with minerals in saliva to become tartar. Tartar is rough, so it holds even more plaque and constantly irritates the gums; once it has formed, brushing won't remove it.

The inner surfaces of the lower front teeth and the cheek side of the upper molars, close to the salivary glands, are where tartar builds up most.

In short

Tartar isn't just cosmetic. Left for a long time, gum inflammation can spread to the bone and teeth start to loosen.

sections.h: How is it done, and does it hurt?
sections.html:
1. Examination and gum measurements
  2. Removing tartar with an ultrasonic tip that breaks it up with vibration and water
  3. Fine cleaning with hand instruments
  4. Polishing the teeth smooth and reducing stains
  5. Advice on brushing and cleaning between teeth

Most people don't find it uncomfortable; you feel water and vibration. If the gums are very inflamed or teeth are sensitive, local anaesthetic or splitting the cleaning into several sessions may be preferred. Where gum pockets are deep, a deep clean of the root surfaces is needed; see gum treatment in Beylikdüzü.

No. Ultrasonic instruments break up hard tartar; used correctly, they don't wear away healthy enamel. The feeling that the gaps between your teeth have "opened up" afterwards comes from the tartar that filled those gaps being removed; the tartar created the space in the first place by pushing the gum back. Details: does teeth cleaning damage enamel.

sections.h: How often should you have it?
sections.html:
Who?Recommended interval
Healthy gums, little tartar build-upEvery 12 months
Most adultsEvery 6 months
Smokers, people with diabetes or a history of gum diseaseEvery 3–4 months
People with braces or implantsAs the dentist recommends, usually every 3–6 months

Combining your cleaning with a check-up also catches decay early. See how often to have a dental check-up.

• Mild cold sensitivity and slight bleeding when brushing are possible for a day or two; they settle as the gums heal.
  • Cutting down on strongly coloured drinks (coffee, tea, red wine) on the first day helps the polish last longer.
  • Keep going with a soft brush, fluoride toothpaste and floss or an interdental brush once a day: how to brush your teeth properly.
  • If bleeding lasts more than a week, you may need gum treatment; come in for a check.

To book, WhatsApp or call +90 555 011 33 68. Dent32 is a dental clinic on the E-5 service road in Beylikdüzü, open every day including weekends.

faq.q: How long does a scale and polish take?
faq.a: Usually 30–45 minutes. With heavy tartar or inflamed gums, more than one session may be needed.

faq.q: Does a scale and polish hurt?
faq.a: For most people it doesn't; you feel water and vibration. Local anaesthetic can be used for sensitive teeth.

faq.q: Why are my teeth sensitive after cleaning?
faq.a: Surfaces previously covered by tartar are exposed, so sensitivity for a day or two is possible. A sensitive-teeth toothpaste helps.

faq.q: Does a scale and polish whiten teeth?
faq.a: It removes stains and tartar, so teeth look lighter, but it doesn't change the tooth's own colour. That needs whitening.

faq.q: Can I have a scale and polish while pregnant?
faq.a: Yes. Gum bleeding can increase in pregnancy, so cleaning is especially recommended; the second trimester is the best time.

title: Private health insurance, complementary insurance and SGK for dental treatment: a payment guide for Beylikdüzü
desc: Does private health insurance, complementary health insurance or SGK cover dental treatment in Turkey? Dental cover, limits, waiting periods, pre-approval, invoices and reimbursement, and payment planning at a private clinic in Beylikdüzü.
seoTitle: Insurance and SGK for dental treatment in Türkiye | Dent32
seoDesc: Does private insurance, complementary insurance or SGK cover dental treatment in Türkiye? Dental cover, limits, pre-approval and reimbursement.
lead: Dental treatment covered by SGK (Turkey's Social Security Institution) is mostly provided at state oral and dental health hospitals and centres; at private clinics, patients usually pay themselves. Private health insurance generally covers dental treatment only if a separate "dental cover" has been added, and only up to the policy limit. Checking your policy before treatment and getting pre-approval from your insurer with a written treatment plan avoids surprises.

sections.html:
Basic dental treatments covered by general health insurance, such as examinations, fillings, extractions and root canal treatment, are mainly provided at Ministry of Health oral and dental hospitals and centres, and at university dental faculties. Conditions such as age and time limits may apply to dentures. Implants and cosmetic treatments are generally not covered.

At private dental clinics, patients usually pay for treatment themselves. Coverage and conditions change from time to time, so we recommend confirming the current rules with SGK or its ALO 170 helpline.

In short

For people who don't want to wait for an appointment at a state facility, or who need treatments that aren't covered, such as implants, zirconia crowns or clear aligners, private clinics with insurance and payment options become the practical choice.

sections.h: Does private health insurance cover dental treatment?
sections.html:
In many private health insurance policies, dental treatment isn't part of the main cover; it's added separately as "dental cover" or an "oral and dental health package". Check these points in your policy:

ItemWhat to check
Scope of coverAre examinations, fillings, root canals, extractions, cleaning, dentures and implants listed individually?
Annual limitThe total amount set aside for dental care and any per-procedure cap
Co-paymentThe percentage of the invoice you pay yourself
Waiting periodHow many months after the policy starts you must wait for each procedure
Contracted providersDirect billing at contracted clinics, or reimbursement against an invoice at non-contracted ones?
Pre-approval (provizyon)Which procedures need approval before treatment

Cosmetic procedures (whitening, veneers, smile design) are excluded from the vast majority of policies.

sections.h: What does complementary health insurance do?
sections.html: Complementary health insurance (tamamlayıcı sağlık sigortası, TSS) is designed to cover the extra fees charged at private hospitals contracted with SGK. Dental treatment isn't part of the main cover in most TSS policies, although some policies can add it as an extra package. Check the "additional cover" section of your policy or ask your insurer.

sections.h: Using insurance for treatment, step by step
sections.html:
1. Have an examination and get a written treatment plan and quote.
  2. Send the plan to your insurer and get written confirmation of which items are covered and how much.
  3. If required, get pre-approval with X-rays and a dentist's report.
  4. After treatment, send your invoice and, if required, X-rays to your insurer.
  5. If the limit is exceeded, discuss spreading treatment across policy years according to urgency.

After the examination, we give you your treatment plan in writing, item by item, and prepare the information and invoice you need for your insurer. Ask when booking which insurers we work with and what payment options are currently available.

If your budget is limited, we split the plan into stages by priority: pain and infection first, then treatments that prevent further loss, and aesthetic work last. We explain what affects prices in dental treatment prices in Beylikdüzü and implant costs in implant cost factors. Contact: +90 555 011 33 68 (WhatsApp and phone).

faq.q: Does private health insurance cover implants?
faq.a: Some comprehensive dental covers pay for implants up to a limit; in most policies they're excluded. Check your policy and limit, and get pre-approval before treatment.

faq.q: Is SGK accepted at private dental clinics?
faq.a: Generally not; dental treatment covered by SGK is mainly provided at state facilities. We recommend confirming the current conditions with SGK.

faq.q: Does complementary insurance pay for dental treatment?
faq.a: Most complementary health insurance policies don't include dental treatment in the main cover; if added as an extra package, it may be covered up to a limit.

faq.q: What documents does my insurer need?
faq.a: Usually an invoice, the treatment plan and, for some procedures, X-rays and a dentist's report. Get your insurer's list in advance.

faq.q: Is teeth whitening covered by insurance?
faq.a: Cosmetic procedures such as whitening, veneers and smile design are excluded from the vast majority of policies.

title: Afraid of the dentist? Step-by-step, unhurried treatment in Beylikdüzü
desc: What causes fear of the dentist (dental anxiety), how to plan a first appointment, comfortable anaesthetic, a "stop" signal, short sessions and practical ways to feel calmer. Dent32's calm approach in Beylikdüzü.
seoTitle: Afraid of the dentist? Unhurried treatment in Beylikdüzü | Dent32
seoDesc: Afraid of the dentist? How to plan a first visit, comfortable anaesthetic, a stop signal, short sessions and practical ways to feel calmer.
lead: Fear of the dentist is very common and often comes from a painful experience in the past. The most effective way to reduce it is to make the first appointment a chance to meet and be examined rather than treated, explain every step in advance and let you stop at any moment. At Dent32, sessions are planned shorter and slower for patients who tell us about their fear up front.

sections.h: Why are people afraid of the dentist?
sections.html:
Dental anxiety affects a large share of adults; for some it becomes a phobia that leads them to avoid appointments altogether. The most common causes are:

  • A painful treatment in childhood or in the past
  • Fear of needles, blood or the sound of the drill
  • Feeling a loss of control and being unable to speak with your mouth open
  • Embarrassment about the state of your teeth and fear of being judged
  • Not knowing how long the treatment will take or what will happen

When fear delays treatment, a small cavity can turn into a root canal and a loose tooth into an extraction. Avoidance creates a cycle that leads to bigger, scarier treatments.

sections.h: How we work with anxious patients at Dent32
sections.html:
• Meet first: At the first appointment we just talk and examine. If you don't feel ready, we don't start treatment that day.
  • Tell, show, do: We explain the instrument we'll use and what you'll feel beforehand, and show it to you if you like.
  • Stop signal: Raise your hand and we stop straight away. This simple rule makes you feel in control.
  • Anaesthetic you barely feel: A numbing gel is applied to the gum first and the anaesthetic is given slowly. We don't start until you're fully numb.
  • Short sessions: We start with short, easy procedures and lengthen sessions as trust builds.
  • No judgement: Not having seen a dentist for a long time isn't something we criticise; it's simply where we start.
In short

Just tell us about your fear when you book. It lets the dentist plan the session around you.

One of our Google reviews sums it up well: "Even people with a fear of dentists like me can go there comfortably. The whole team is friendly and helpful in every situation." (Tülay Ç.) Another patient wrote that they didn't feel the slightest pain during two extractions and praised the gentle care for patients' sensitivities (Haluk M.). You can read more reviews on our Google Maps listing.

sections.h: Practical tips before and during your appointment
sections.html:
• Book in the morning or early in the day; waiting all day increases anxiety.
  • Cut down on caffeine before your appointment.
  • Bring someone you trust.
  • Listening to music or a podcast on headphones drowns out the drill.
  • Breathe slowly: in through your nose for 4 seconds, out through your mouth for 6.
  • Ask how long it will take; a procedure with a known length is easier to get through.

For children, making the first visit pain-free and playful is key to preventing fear; see dental care for children in Beylikdüzü.

sections.h: Haven't been for years? Where to start
sections.html:
The best start is an examination while you're not in pain and, if needed, a scale and polish. That way you learn the state of your mouth and get used to the clinic with a painless procedure. Treatments are then put in order of urgency. We explain how the examination goes in our dental check-up guide.

Just mention your fear when you message us on WhatsApp to book: +90 555 011 33 68. Dent32 is a dental clinic in Barış, Beylikdüzü, on the E-5 service road, open every day including weekends.

faq.q: How can I overcome my fear of the dentist?
faq.a: A first appointment just to meet and be examined, explaining every step in advance, being able to stop at any moment and short sessions are the most effective ways to build trust.

faq.q: Does the anaesthetic injection hurt?
faq.a: A numbing gel is applied first and the anaesthetic is given slowly; most patients feel only slight pressure.

faq.q: I haven't been to a dentist for years and feel embarrassed. What should I do?
faq.a: This is something we see very often. We examine without judgement and agree the priorities with you.

faq.q: Do I have to have treatment at the first appointment?
faq.a: No. If you don't feel ready, the first appointment can be limited to an examination and planning.

faq.q: Can someone come with me?

sections.h: What do the rating and number of reviews tell you?

As for ratings, the difference between 5.0 and 4.7 is often not meaningful; what matters is the content and consistency of recent reviews.

title: Dental treatment for older adults in Beylikdüzü: dentures, implants, medicines and dry mouth
desc: Dental treatment for people aged 65 and over: dentures and implant-retained dentures, blood thinners and bone medicines, dry mouth, root decay, denture care and advice for family members. Dent32 Beylikdüzü.
seoTitle: Dental treatment for older adults in Beylikdüzü | Dent32
seoDesc: Dental care at 65 and over: dentures and implant dentures, blood thinners and bone medicines, dry mouth, root decay and denture care.
lead: Older age on its own isn't a barrier to implants or dental treatment; what matters is general health, medicines and the state of the bone. The most common problems in this age group are loose or uncomfortable dentures, decay on root surfaces and dry mouth caused by medicines. Giving the dentist a complete list of your medicines before treatment is the first step to safe planning.

sections.h: Common mouth problems in later life
sections.html:
ProblemCauseWhat can be done
Loose denturesBone gradually shrinking after tooth lossRelining, a new denture or securing it with implants

• Blood thinners: Aspirin, warfarin and newer anticoagulants affect bleeding during procedures such as extractions. Don't stop them yourself; the decision is made with the doctor who prescribed them.

Bringing your medicine boxes or prescription list to the appointment is the easiest way to help the dentist plan safely.

Securing a loose lower full denture with two or four implants can make a big difference to quality of life. The denture clicks onto the implants, making chewing and speaking more comfortable. sections.h: Home care and tips for family members
sections.html:
• If manual dexterity is reduced, an electric toothbrush or a thick-handled brush makes things easier.
  • Dentures should be taken out and brushed every evening, and kept overnight in water or water with a cleaning tablet.
  • Gently brush the gums under the denture with a soft brush too.
  • Fluoride toothpaste (including high-fluoride toothpaste if your dentist recommends it) reduces root decay.
  • If you care for a relative's teeth, brushing from behind with their head supported can help.
  • Everyone, including people with no teeth who wear dentures, should have a check-up at least once a year; denture fit and mouth sores are picked up at these visits.

sections.h: Planning for older patients at Dent32
