title: Zirconia crowns in Beylikdüzü: how many visits, who they suit and what affects the price
desc: Zirconia crowns in Beylikdüzü, Istanbul: who they suit, how many visits and days they take, how much the tooth is reduced, how long they last and what affects the price.
seoTitle: Zirconia crowns in Beylikdüzü: visits, suitability, cost | Dent32
seoDesc: Zirconia crowns in Beylikdüzü: who they suit, how many visits they take, how much tooth is reduced, how long they last and price factors.
lead: A zirconia crown is a strong, metal-free cap bonded over a worn, broken, discoloured or root-filled tooth. From examination to fitting, most patients need 3–4 appointments over about 1–2 weeks.

sections.html:
Zirconia is a high-strength ceramic. With no metal underneath, there's no dark line at the gum edge and light passes through in a way close to a natural tooth. That's why it's widely used for both front and back teeth.

For back teeth that carry chewing loads, solid (monolithic) zirconia is usually chosen; for front teeth, porcelain can be layered on top for a more lifelike look. We compare materials in our types of dental crowns article.

• Teeth weakened or broken by large fillings
  • Back teeth that need strengthening after root canal treatment
  • Severe discolouration that doesn't respond to whitening
  • Bridges to replace a missing tooth, or crowns on implants
  • People replacing old metal-backed crowns

If the tooth is largely sound and only the front surface needs an aesthetic change, a laminate veneer, which needs less reduction, may be a better choice.

sections.h: How many visits and how many days?
sections.html:
StageWhat happensTypical time
1. Examination and planX-rays, gum and bite check, colour and shape plan1 visit
2. Preparation and impressionsTeeth are reduced under local anaesthetic, impressions taken, temporary crowns fitted1 visit (1–2 hours)
3. Try-inThe framework or crown is tried in; colour and fit are checked1 visit
4. FittingCrowns are permanently bonded and the bite adjusted1 visit

The lab work between impressions and fitting usually takes 5–10 working days. It takes longer if root canal treatment, fillings or gum treatment are needed first. Because we're open at weekends, it's easier to fit appointments around your work.

In short

On healthy teeth, zirconia crowns are usually completed in 1–2 weeks over 3–4 visits.

sections.h: How much is the tooth reduced? Does it hurt?
sections.html:
For a zirconia crown, roughly 1–1.5 mm is usually removed around the tooth, more than for a veneer. It's done under local anaesthetic, so no pain is expected. There may be some hot and cold sensitivity for a few days afterwards; the temporary crown protects the tooth meanwhile.

We explain what sensitivity is normal in our sensitivity after crowns article.

FactorExplanation
Number of teethA single tooth, a few teeth or a full smile plan
Type of zirconiaMonolithic or porcelain-layered; front and back teeth have different needs
Preliminary treatmentWhether root canal treatment, fillings or gum treatment are needed
Aesthetic expectationsExtra lab work for colour and surface detail on front teeth
On an implant?Implant crowns also include connecting parts

We give every item in writing after the examination. General price factors are covered in our dental treatment prices in Beylikdüzü article.

sections.h: How long do zirconia crowns last?
sections.html:
Well-planned, well-maintained zirconia crowns can last many years. The main factors are the health of the tooth underneath, keeping the gum edge clean and whether you clench or grind. If you grind at night, a night guard protects your crowns.

You can see unretouched cases in our gallery and book at our dental clinic in Beylikdüzü to discuss your own situation.

faq.q: Can zirconia crowns be done within a week?
faq.a: If no preliminary treatment is needed, 5–10 working days between impressions and fitting is enough for most patients. Root canal or gum treatment adds time.

faq.q: Do zirconia crowns change colour over time?
faq.a: No. Zirconia and porcelain surfaces don't stain permanently from tea, coffee or smoking, although surrounding natural teeth and the gum edge can.

faq.q: Should I whiten my teeth before getting crowns?
faq.a: The crown colour is matched to neighbouring natural teeth. If you want lighter teeth, whiten first; crowns don't whiten afterwards.

faq.q: Can a crowned tooth decay?
faq.a: The crown itself can't, but natural tooth at the gum edge can. Floss, interdental brushes and regular check-ups reduce the risk.

faq.q: Zirconia or porcelain?
faq.a: Compared with metal-backed porcelain, zirconia is more aesthetic and kinder to the gums. The choice depends on the tooth's position, bite forces and aesthetic expectations, and is made at the examination.

title: Smile design in Beylikdüzü: planning, try-in and treatment step by step
desc: How smile design works at a dental clinic in Beylikdüzü, Istanbul: digital planning, mock-up try-in, veneers, zirconia, orthodontics and gum contouring, timelines and cost factors.
seoTitle: Smile design in Beylikdüzü: planning and try-in | Dent32
seoDesc: How smile design works: digital planning, mock-up try-in, veneers, zirconia, orthodontics and gum contouring, timelines and cost factors.
lead: Smile design means planning the length, shape and colour of your teeth and the gum line to suit your face, and trying it in your mouth before any treatment. The plan is usually a combination of veneers or zirconia crowns, whitening, orthodontics and gum contouring.

sections.h: Is smile design a single procedure?
sections.html:
No. Smile design isn't a treatment but a planning method. Your face, lips and teeth are analysed together, then the least invasive procedures that reach the target smile are chosen. For some patients whitening and bonding are enough; others need orthodontics first, then crowns.

We explain the general approach in what is smile design; here we focus on how the process runs at our clinic in Beylikdüzü.

sections.h: Which procedures can be part of the plan?
sections.html:
ProcedureWhat it doesTooth reduction
Teeth whiteningLightens natural teethNone
BondingSmall chips, gaps and shape correctionsNone or minimal
Laminate veneersChange shape, colour and length of front teethLittle (about 0.3–0.7 mm)
Zirconia crownsFully cover weak, broken or very discoloured teethMore
Clear aligner orthodonticsCorrects crowding, may reduce the need for crownsNone
Gum contouringBalances a gummy smile and asymmetryNone

1. Examination and photos: Clinical examination, X-rays and face and smile photos; we discuss your expectations.
  2. Digital plan: Tooth lengths, midline, smile line and colour options are planned.
  3. Mock-up try-in: The planned smile is recreated on your teeth with a temporary material; you see it in the mirror and in photos and can ask for changes.
  4. Approval and written plan: What will be done to each tooth, the timeline and the cost are given in writing.
  5. Treatment: The approved plan is carried out through whitening, orthodontics, veneers or zirconia.
  6. Review: Bite, speech and gum fit are checked; a night guard may be recommended.
Why the try-in matters

The hard-to-reverse step in smile design is tooth reduction. A mock-up lets you see the result before you decide and avoids unnecessary reduction.

sections.h: Orthodontics first, or straight to veneers?
sections.html:
If teeth are crowded or tilted, aligning them with veneers means removing more tooth. In that case, a few months of clear aligners to straighten the teeth first, followed by veneers with less reduction, is often the more conservative route.

Our founder, Dr. Hüseyin Aşçı, works in orthodontics and aesthetic dentistry, so we assess both stages in a single plan. See orthodontics in Beylikdüzü for more.

sections.h: How long does smile design take?
sections.html:
Type of planTypical time
Whitening + bonding1–2 visits
Veneers or zirconia crownsAbout 1–2 weeks, 3–4 visits
Orthodontics first, then veneersA few months to a year, depending on orthodontics
With gum contouringAdd a few weeks for healing

Cost depends on the procedures, the number of teeth and materials. After the examination and try-in we give you an itemised written plan. To get started, book an appointment at Dent32, our dental clinic in Beylikdüzü.

faq.q: How many teeth are included in smile design?
faq.a: It depends on how many teeth show when you smile; most plans involve 6 to 10 upper teeth. The number is set after photo analysis and the try-in.

faq.q: Does smile design look natural?
faq.a: It depends on how well tooth proportions suit your face, the colour chosen and surface detail. The try-in shows you beforehand whether the result suits you.

faq.q: Is there an age limit?
faq.a: Teeth and gums need to have finished developing, usually around 18. There's no upper limit; what matters is the health of the teeth and gums.

faq.q: Can I change my mind after the try-in?
faq.a: Yes. The mock-up uses a temporary material and nothing permanent is done to your teeth. Treatment doesn't start without your approval.

title: Teeth whitening in Beylikdüzü: one session in the clinic or trays at home?
desc: Teeth whitening in Beylikdüzü, Istanbul: in-clinic versus at-home whitening, number of sessions, sensitivity, how long results last, who it isn't suitable for and aftercare.
seoTitle: Teeth whitening in Beylikdüzü: clinic or at home? | Dent32
seoDesc: In-clinic versus at-home teeth whitening: number of sessions, sensitivity, how long results last, who it doesn't suit and aftercare.
lead: Teeth whitening lightens tooth colour with peroxide gels under a dentist's supervision, either in a single session of about an hour in the clinic or with custom trays at home over 1–2 weeks. Depending on habits, results usually last 1–3 years.

sections.html:
Whitening works well on natural teeth yellowed by tea, coffee, smoking or age. Results can be more limited for antibiotic (tetracycline) or fluorosis staining; in those cases options such as veneers or bonding are discussed.

Important

Artificial surfaces such as fillings, crowns and veneers don't whiten. If you have old fillings in your front teeth, they may need replacing after whitening; we plan this from the start.

sections.h: In the clinic or at home?
sections.html:
In-clinic (in-office)At-home
How it's doneGums are protected with a barrier and gel is applied to the teethA lower-strength gel is used in custom clear trays
TimeA single session of about 1 hourA set time each day for about 1–2 weeks
ResultsSame dayGradual
SensitivityMay be temporary for a few daysUsually milder
Best forPeople who want fast resultsPeople who can apply it regularly; top-ups

For some patients we combine the two: starting in the clinic and maintaining the result with home trays, or topping up over the years. See teeth whitening: clinic or home? for general information.

• Examination: Decay, leaking filling edges or gum recession are treated first; otherwise sensitivity increases.
  • Scale and polish: Whitening over tartar and surface stains gives uneven results. Professional cleaning is usually done a few days before.
  • Shade record: Your starting shade is recorded so you can compare the result.

Teeth pick up colour more easily for the first 24–48 hours. During this time we recommend avoiding tea, coffee, cola, red wine, dark sauces and smoking. A toothpaste for sensitive teeth helps with temporary sensitivity.

How long the result lasts depends largely on habits. Regular cleaning and short home top-ups when needed keep the colour for a long time.

• Pregnant and breastfeeding women
  • Teenagers whose teeth haven't finished developing (generally under 16–18)
  • People with untreated decay or active gum disease
  • People with severe sensitivity due to marked gum recession and exposed roots

A short examination at our dental clinic in Beylikdüzü will tell us if whitening suits you. If you'd like to change your smile as a whole, take a look at smile design.

faq.q: Does whitening damage enamel?
faq.a: Whitening done under a dentist's supervision at the right strength doesn't permanently damage enamel. The risk lies mostly with overusing unsupervised products bought online.

faq.q: How many shades lighter will my teeth get?
faq.a: It depends on the starting shade and type of staining. Promising an exact shade in advance isn't honest; we record your shade together at the start.

faq.q: Does whitening hurt?
faq.a: No pain is expected during treatment. Some patients get brief, sharp twinges for 1–2 days afterwards that usually settle on their own.

faq.q: Will my crowns whiten too?
faq.a: No. Crowns, veneers and fillings don't whiten. If they're visible, they may need replacing to match the new shade.

faq.q: How often can it be repeated?
faq.a: For most patients the first result lasts for years. Short top-ups with home trays can be done if needed; frequent in-clinic sessions aren't recommended.

title: Orthodontics in Beylikdüzü: clear aligners and braces, timelines and check-ups
desc: Orthodontic treatment in Beylikdüzü, Istanbul: how clear aligners and braces work, who they suit, how long treatment takes, a child's first orthodontic check and retention afterwards.
seoTitle: Orthodontics in Beylikdüzü: clear aligners and braces | Dent32
seoDesc: Clear aligners and braces in Beylikdüzü: how they work, who they suit, how long treatment takes, a child's first check and retention.
lead: Orthodontics straightens crowded, gapped or misaligned teeth with clear aligners or braces. For adults, treatment usually takes between 6 months and 2 years, and a retainer is worn afterwards to keep teeth in place.

sections.html:
• Crowded or gapped teeth
  • Upper teeth sitting too far forward, or lower teeth biting in front
  • Deep bite, open bite and crossbite
  • Cases where teeth need moving into position before crowns, veneers or implants

Orthodontics isn't only about looks. Misaligned teeth are harder to clean, which increases the risk of decay and gum disease.

With clear aligners, tooth movements are planned on a digital model and a series of aligners is made, each moving the teeth a small amount. Aligners are worn about 20–22 hours a day, removed for eating and brushing, and changed at intervals set by the dentist.

Small tooth-coloured bumps (attachments) are bonded to some teeth to help the aligners grip. Success depends largely on wearing them consistently.

Clear alignersBraces
AppearanceAlmost invisibleMetal or tooth-coloured ceramic brackets
EatingRemove aligners and eat normallyCare needed with hard and sticky food
CleaningNormal brushing and flossingExtra care around brackets

See clear aligners vs braces for a detailed comparison.

sections.h: When should a child have a first orthodontic check?
sections.html:
Orthodontists recommend a child's first orthodontic assessment at around age 7. Treatment doesn't always start then, but jaw growth problems and crowding spotted early can often be guided with simpler appliances.

Other topics for children are covered in our dental care for children in Beylikdüzü article.

sections.h: How long does it take and how often are check-ups?
sections.html:
SituationTypical time
Mild crowding or gapsAbout 6–12 months
Moderate casesAbout 12–18 months
Complex bite problems18–24 months or longer

Check-ups are usually every 4–8 weeks depending on the treatment. Since the clinic is open seven days a week, you can book them outside work or school hours, including weekends.

Once treatment ends, teeth tend to drift back. That's why a clear or fixed retainer is used; wearing it consistently is especially important in the first year.

Our founder, Dr. Hüseyin Aşçı, works in orthodontics and aesthetic dentistry. Where needed, we plan orthodontics together with smile design, crowns or implants. General information is on our clear aligner orthodontics page, and you can book an examination at our dental clinic in Beylikdüzü.

faq.q: Can adults have orthodontic treatment?
faq.a: Yes. If teeth and gums are healthy, there's no age limit. Adults often choose clear aligners because they're nearly invisible.

faq.q: Do clear aligners affect speech?
faq.a: There may be a slight lisp for the first few days; most patients adapt quickly.

faq.q: Can I eat with aligners in?
faq.a: No. Remove them before eating, brush your teeth afterwards and put them back in. It's also best to remove them when drinking anything other than water.

faq.q: Does orthodontic treatment hurt?
faq.a: You may feel pressure and tenderness for 1–2 days after switching aligners or adjusting braces. It shows the teeth are moving and soon passes.

faq.q: How long should I wear my retainer?
faq.a: Longer at first, then usually only at night. Long-term use is recommended to keep teeth in place.

title: Dental care for children in Beylikdüzü: first visit, preventive care and fear-free treatment
desc: For families looking for a dentist for their child in Beylikdüzü, Istanbul: when to have the first dental visit, fluoride varnish and fissure sealants, why baby teeth should be treated, and how to ease a child's fear of the dentist.
seoTitle: Dental care for children in Beylikdüzü | Dent32
seoDesc: Your child's first dental visit, fluoride varnish and fissure sealants, why baby teeth are treated, and easing a child's fear of the dentist.
lead: A child's first dental visit should be when the first baby tooth appears, or by their first birthday at the latest. Regular check-ups and preventive care such as fluoride varnish and fissure sealants prevent most decay in baby and adult teeth.

sections.h: When should the first visit be?
sections.html:
The first baby tooth usually appears at around 6 months. A first visit then, or by age 1, is mainly to guide parents on feeding, bottle and dummy habits and brushing. Regular visits from an early age mean a child gets to know the dentist through routine check-ups rather than pain.

We describe how the first visit goes in your child's first dental visit.

TreatmentWhat it doesWhen?
Fluoride varnishStrengthens enamel and slows early decay2–4 times a year depending on risk
Fissure sealantsSeal the deep grooves on the chewing surfaces of molarsAfter adult molars erupt (around ages 6 and 12)
Regular check-upsCatch decay while it's smallUsually every 6 months
Brushing guidanceTeaches the right technique and amount of fluorideAt every visit

sections.h: Baby teeth fall out anyway, so why treat them?
sections.html:
• Pain and infection: Untreated decay reaches the nerve, causing pain and abscesses.
  • Effect on adult teeth: Infection at the root of a baby tooth can affect the adult tooth developing underneath.
  • Holding space: If a baby tooth is lost early, the gap can close and the adult tooth comes in crooked. A space maintainer may be needed.
  • Eating and speech: Painful teeth make chewing and some sounds harder.

sections.h: How can a child's fear of the dentist be eased?
sections.html:
With children, we first introduce the instruments and the procedure in age-appropriate language, then show, then do (tell-show-do). Short appointments that end on a positive note make the next visit easier.

  • Don't present the visit as a reward or punishment, and avoid phrases like "it won't hurt" that can create anxiety.
  • Choose a time when your child isn't tired or hungry.
  • Try not to pass on your own dental anxiety.

Dent32 has a colourful treatment room designed for children. As the clinic is open at weekends, appointments can be planned without missing school.

SituationWhat to do
An adult tooth is knocked outHold the tooth by the crown, not the root; rinse briefly with water if dirty, keep it in milk and come in immediately. The first hour is critical.
A tooth is brokenKeep the broken piece, rinse the mouth with warm water and come in the same day.
Facial swelling and feverThis may be infection; see a dentist without delay.
A baby tooth is knocked outBaby teeth aren't put back, but the surrounding tissues still need checking.

See our children's dentistry page for more, and book an appointment at Dent32, our dental clinic in Beylikdüzü.

faq.q: When should children start brushing?
faq.a: From the first tooth. Use a smear (rice-grain size) of fluoride toothpaste up to age 3 and a pea-sized amount from 3 to 6; parents should brush or supervise until about 7–8.

faq.q: Do fissure sealants harm the tooth?
faq.a: No. A sealant is a flowable material applied without drilling. It's painless and needs no anaesthetic.

faq.q: Can baby teeth have root canal treatment?
faq.a: Yes. When decay reaches the nerve of a baby tooth, a pulpotomy or baby-tooth root canal treatment can save it.

faq.q: What if my child won't cooperate?
faq.a: We first build trust with familiarisation visits. Sometimes treatment is split into several short sessions; for extensive treatment where cooperation isn't possible, we can refer for advanced sedation options.

title: Root canal treatment in Beylikdüzü: symptoms, number of visits and aftercare
desc: Root canal treatment in Beylikdüzü, Istanbul: which symptoms mean you need one, how many visits it takes, whether it hurts, whether you need a crown afterwards and what to do about weekend toothache.
seoTitle: Root canal treatment in Beylikdüzü | Dent32
seoDesc: Which symptoms mean you need a root canal, how many visits it takes, whether it hurts, whether you need a crown, and weekend toothache.
lead: Root canal treatment cleans out an inflamed nerve damaged by decay or trauma and seals the canals so the tooth can be kept. It's done under local anaesthetic and most teeth are finished in 1–2 visits.

sections.h: Which symptoms point to a root canal?
sections.html:
• Lingering pain after hot or cold
  • Spontaneous, throbbing pain that wakes you at night
  • Pain when biting or touching the tooth
  • A pimple-like bump on the gum (fistula) or facial swelling
  • A tooth that darkens after an injury

Sometimes the nerve dies without symptoms and the problem only shows on an X-ray. The decision is made after examination and X-rays.

1. The tooth is numbed with local anaesthetic and isolated from saliva.
  2. Decay is removed and the pulp chamber is reached.
  3. The canals are cleaned and shaped with fine instruments and rinsed with disinfecting solutions.
  4. Canal lengths are checked with X-rays or an electronic device.
  5. The canals are filled with a permanent material and the tooth is sealed.
How many visits?

Without infection, most teeth are done in one visit. With an abscess or severe inflammation, medication may be placed in the canals and the filling done at a second visit.

With effective anaesthesia you won't feel pain during treatment; only pressure and vibration. The tooth may be tender to bite on for 2–3 days afterwards; that's normal and painkillers help. If pain keeps increasing or swelling develops, contact the clinic.

General information is in our when do you need a root canal article.

sections.h: Do you need a crown afterwards?
sections.html:
ToothGeneral advice
Front teeth, little tooth lossA composite filling is often enough
Premolars and molarsA crown is usually recommended to prevent fracture
Teeth with major lossA post and crown may be needed

Root-filled teeth become more brittle over time. On back teeth, a zirconia crown protects against fracture and helps the tooth last.

sections.h: What if the root canal fails?
sections.html: Root canal treatment has a high success rate, but infection can return years later. Re-treatment is tried first; if needed, root-end surgery (apicectomy) is done. If the tooth can't be saved, it's extracted and replaced with an implant or bridge.

sections.h: When toothache starts at the weekend
sections.html: Pain that needs a root canal often starts at the worst time: at night or at the weekend. Dent32 is open seven days a week, so we can see a painful tooth the same day and, if needed, carry out first aid (opening the tooth to relieve pressure). Message us on WhatsApp before coming to our dental clinic in Beylikdüzü to cut your waiting time.

faq.q: How long does a root canal take?
faq.a: Usually 30–60 minutes for front teeth and 60–90 minutes for multi-canal molars, depending on the number of canals and inflammation.

faq.q: Can antibiotics replace a root canal?
faq.a: No. Antibiotics can help control spreading infection and swelling, but they don't clean out the inflamed tissue inside the tooth. Pain may ease temporarily but the problem remains.

faq.q: Will a root-filled tooth last for life?
faq.a: A properly treated and well-restored tooth can last many years, often for life.

faq.q: Root canal or extraction?
faq.a: Keeping the natural tooth is preferred where possible. If the tooth is badly broken or the root is cracked, extraction and an implant may be more predictable; the decision is made at the examination.

title: Gum treatment in Beylikdüzü: bleeding, recession and deep cleaning
desc: Gum treatment in Beylikdüzü, Istanbul: causes of bleeding and receding gums, gingivitis versus periodontitis, deep cleaning, the effect of smoking and diabetes, home care and check-up intervals.
seoTitle: Gum treatment in Beylikdüzü: bleeding and recession | Dent32
seoDesc: Bleeding and receding gums: gingivitis versus periodontitis, deep cleaning, the effect of smoking and diabetes, home care and check-ups.
lead: Bleeding gums are the earliest sign of gum disease. At the early stage (gingivitis) it reverses fully with professional cleaning and good home care; at the advanced stage (periodontitis), deep cleaning and regular maintenance stop it progressing.

sections.html:
• Bleeding when brushing or flossing
  • Red, swollen, tender gums
  • Persistent bad breath or a bad taste
  • Receding gums and teeth that look longer
  • Loose teeth or widening gaps

In smokers, gum blood vessels constrict so bleeding is less visible, which can delay diagnosis.

GingivitisPeriodontitis
Tissue affectedGums onlyGums, supporting tissue and bone
SignsBleeding, rednessRecession, pockets, looseness, bone loss
Reversible?FullyLost bone usually doesn't return; progression is stopped
TreatmentScale and polish plus home careDeep cleaning, surgery if needed, regular maintenance

1. Examination and charting: Pocket depths are measured and bone levels assessed on X-rays.
  2. Scale and polish: Tartar and plaque are removed from the tooth surfaces and polished.
  3. Deep cleaning (root planing): Tartar below the gum line is removed under local anaesthetic and root surfaces smoothed.
  4. Re-evaluation: The gum response is measured after a few weeks; if deep pockets remain, surgical options are discussed.
  5. Maintenance: Check-ups and cleaning, usually every 3–6 months depending on risk.

Smoking and uncontrolled diabetes are the strongest risk factors for gum disease: they speed it up and reduce the response to treatment. The link with diabetes works both ways: treating gum inflammation can also help blood sugar control.

A similar inflammation (peri-implantitis) can develop around implants, so implant aftercare and regular check-ups matter.

• Brushing twice a day for two minutes with a soft brush
  • Floss or correctly sized interdental brushes between teeth
  • Short-term antiseptic mouthwash when your dentist recommends it
  • Stopping or cutting down smoking

We explain the causes in more detail in bleeding and receding gums. You can book a gum check at our dental clinic in Beylikdüzü.

faq.q: Will bleeding gums stop on their own?
faq.a: Usually not, unless the plaque and tartar causing it are removed. Stopping brushing makes it worse; keep brushing gently and come in for a check.

faq.q: Do receded gums grow back?
faq.a: Not on their own. Progression can be stopped, and in suitable cases surgery such as a gum graft can cover the exposed root.

faq.q: Does deep cleaning hurt?
faq.a: It's done under local anaesthetic, so no pain is expected during treatment. There may be some tenderness for a few days.

faq.q: Can gum disease cause tooth loss?
faq.a: Yes. Advanced periodontitis is one of the main causes of tooth loss in adults. Early treatment is the most effective way to keep your teeth.

title: Laminate veneers in Beylikdüzü: who they suit and how many visits they take
desc: Porcelain laminate veneers in Beylikdüzü, Istanbul: who they suit and who they don't, how much tooth is reduced, how many visits they take, and veneers versus zirconia and bonding.
seoTitle: Laminate veneers in Beylikdüzü | Dent32
seoDesc: Porcelain veneers: who they suit, how much tooth is reduced, how many visits they take, and veneers versus zirconia crowns and bonding.
lead: Laminate veneers are thin ceramic shells, about 0.3–0.7 mm thick, bonded to the front surface of the teeth. They change shape, colour and length with minimal reduction, and most patients are finished in 2–3 visits over about 1–2 weeks.

sections.html:
A veneer is a thin restoration, usually made from glass ceramics such as e.max, that lets light through much like natural enamel. Unlike a zirconia crown, it covers only the front of the tooth, so far less tooth is removed.

See what are laminate veneers for general information.

Veneers may still be possible in these cases, but a night guard, orthodontics or a different restoration is discussed first. If your teeth are crowded, aligning them with clear aligners first can reduce the reduction needed.

1. Examination and smile analysis: Photos are taken and tooth and gum health checked.
  2. Mock-up try-in: The planned shape is tried on your teeth with a temporary material.
  3. Preparation and impressions: The minimum necessary reduction is done, impressions are taken and temporary veneers fitted.
  4. Bonding: After checking colour and fit, the veneers are permanently bonded with special adhesives.

Including planning and try-in, the process is usually 2–3 visits over about 1–2 weeks. In some cases no-prep veneers, with little or no reduction, are possible.

sections.h: How long do veneers last and how do you look after them?
sections.html:
Well-planned, well-maintained veneers can last many years. Not biting hard objects (nutshells, pens, nails) with your front teeth, wearing a night guard if you grind, and six-monthly check-ups all extend their life.

See cases in our gallery and book an examination and try-in at Dent32, our dental clinic in Beylikdüzü.

faq.q: Is the whole tooth cut down for a veneer?
faq.a: No. Only about 0.3–0.7 mm is removed from the front surface; in some cases no reduction is needed.

faq.q: Can veneers fall off?
faq.a: Properly bonded veneers don't come off easily. Biting hard objects with front teeth and grinding at night increase the risk of chipping or debonding.

faq.q: Will my teeth be sensitive after veneers?
faq.a: When reduction stays within the enamel, sensitivity is usually mild and temporary.

faq.q: Can I choose any shade I like?
faq.a: Yes, a wide range of shades is possible. For a natural look we suggest a shade that suits your skin tone, the whites of your eyes and your gums; we decide together at the try-in.

title: What determines dental treatment prices in Beylikdüzü? (2026)
desc: What affects the price of fillings, root canals, zirconia crowns, veneers, implants and orthodontics in Beylikdüzü, Istanbul: the Turkish Dental Association fee schedule, insurance, written treatment plans and the hidden cost of cheap treatment.
seoDesc: What affects the price of fillings, root canals, crowns, veneers, implants and orthodontics: the TDB fee schedule, insurance and written plans.
lead: Dental prices depend on the type of treatment, the number of teeth, the materials used and whether extra procedures are needed. That's why an accurate price can only be given after an examination and any necessary imaging, as an itemised written plan.

sections.h: Why can't you just give one price?
sections.html:
The answer to "how much is a root canal?" depends on whether it's a front tooth or a molar, how many canals it has and whether it will be finished with a filling or a crown. With implants, everything from the brand to bone grafting comes into play. A single figure given over the phone often changes after the examination.

That's why, at Dent32, we share the findings, options and the cost of each item in writing after the examination.

We cover implant costs in detail in what affects implant prices.

sections.h: What is the TDB minimum fee schedule?
sections.html:
Each year the Turkish Dental Association (TDB) publishes a minimum fee schedule for dentists in private practice. It sets a floor for procedures; clinics set their own prices above it according to materials and service.

If a quote is far below the schedule, ask specifically which materials will be used and what is and isn't included in the plan.

• Private health insurance: Some policies cover certain dental treatments. Check the scope and limits with your policy or insurer.
  • SGK (Turkish social security): SGK-covered dental treatment is generally provided at public oral and dental health centres; at private clinics, fees are usually paid by the patient.
  • Payment options: For longer treatments, ask how payment can be arranged when you book.

sections.h: The hidden cost of cheap treatment
sections.html:
The most expensive dental treatment is the one that has to be redone. An ill-fitting crown can lead to gum disease, an incompletely cleaned canal to re-infection, and a poorly positioned implant to bone loss. In those cases, the cost of re-treatment is added to what you paid first.

lead: Dentures restore chewing, speech and appearance when many or all teeth are missing. They can be removable or fixed to implants; removable dentures are usually completed in 4–5 visits.

sections.html:
TypeFor whom?Features
Full dentureNo teeth left in one jawRests on the palate and gums; retention depends on mouth anatomy
Partial dentureSome teeth missingClasps onto remaining teeth
Cobalt-chrome or precision-attachment denturePeople wanting a thinner, more aesthetic partial dentureUses a metal framework or hidden attachments

We cover implant options separately in implant-supported dentures and All-on-Four.

1. Examination: Oral tissues and remaining teeth are assessed; extractions or fillings are done first if needed.
  2. Impressions: Precise impressions are taken with a custom tray.
  3. Bite and tooth selection: The jaw relationship is recorded; tooth shade and shape are chosen to suit your face.
  4. Try-in: Teeth set in wax are tried in; appearance and speech are checked.
  5. Fitting and reviews: The denture is fitted; sore spots are adjusted over the first weeks.

A new denture can feel large and foreign at first. Slight changes in speech, extra saliva and sore spots are normal. Most people adapt within 2–4 weeks.

  • In the first days, eat soft food in small bites, chewing on both sides together.
  • Reading aloud helps you get used to speaking.
  • If you get a sore spot, don't file the denture yourself; come in for an adjustment.

• Take it out after every meal and brush it under running water; use soap or denture cleaner rather than toothpaste.
  • Take it out at night and store it in clean water or a cleaning-tablet solution so your tissues can rest.
  • Don't use hot water; it can warp the denture.
  • Clean your palate, tongue and gums with a soft brush too.

After tooth loss, the jawbone gradually shrinks, so a denture that fits well at first can loosen over the years. It then needs relining or replacing. A loose denture causes sores and chewing problems, so a yearly check is recommended.

If you're unhappy with a removable denture, see dental implants in Beylikdüzü for implant-supported options, and book an examination at our dental clinic in Beylikdüzü.

faq.q: Can I eat everything with dentures?
faq.a: Once you're used to them, most foods. Very hard, sticky and seeded foods can be difficult; implant-retained dentures significantly increase chewing power.

faq.q: Should I use denture adhesive?
faq.a: A well-fitting denture often doesn't need adhesive. If you always need it, your denture may need relining or replacing.

faq.q: Can a denture be fitted right after extraction?
faq.a: Yes, an immediate denture can be fitted the same day. As the tissues heal the fit changes, so relining or a permanent denture is needed later.

faq.q: How long do dentures last?
faq.a: Depending on changes in your mouth and wear, a check every few years and replacement when needed is recommended.

lead: A dental examination means listening to your concerns, examining the whole mouth and gums, taking X-rays if needed and explaining the findings to you. Most adults are advised to have a check-up every 6 months; depending on risk, this can range from 3 to 12 months.

sections.html: Decay and gum disease often cause no pain at first. Decay caught early can be fixed with a simple filling; once pain starts, a root canal and crown may be needed. Regular check-ups mean simpler and less costly treatment.

1. Medical history: You're asked about medicines, chronic conditions, allergies and pregnancy.
  2. Your concerns: We discuss pain, sensitivity or aesthetic goals.
  3. Clinical examination: All teeth, fillings, crowns, gums, tongue, cheeks and palate are examined.
  4. Gum measurements: Pocket depths are measured if needed.
  5. Imaging: X-rays or a 3D CT scan if needed.
  6. Findings and plan: We show you what we found and share the options and approximate cost in writing.

ImagingWhen it's used
Periapical (small) X-rayA single tooth's root, root canal treatment and infection checks

Panoramic X-rayAn overview of all teeth, jaws and impacted teeth

faq.q: How long does an examination take?

faq.q: Can I see a dentist while pregnant?
faq.a: Yes, and you should. Gum inflammation is more common in pregnancy. The second trimester is generally best for routine treatment; X-rays are taken only if needed, with protection.

title: Choosing a dental clinic in Beylikdüzü, Istanbul: what to look for
desc: How to choose a dental clinic in Beylikdüzü or anywhere in Istanbul: the examination, a written treatment plan and price, the dental team, sterilisation, access and aftercare.
seoTitle: Choosing a dental clinic in Beylikdüzü, Istanbul | Dent32
seoDesc: How to choose a dental clinic in Beylikdüzü or Istanbul: the examination, a written plan and price, the team, sterilisation and aftercare.
lead: The quickest way to judge a dental clinic in Beylikdüzü is to look at how thorough the first examination is, whether the treatment plan and cost are given in writing, and how follow-up is handled after treatment.

sections.h: Why does choosing the right clinic matter?
sections.html:
Many dental treatments are hard to reverse: enamel that is removed doesn't grow back, an extracted tooth can't be put back, and an implant can't easily be repositioned once it's in the bone. That's why the quality of planning should weigh as much as price or convenience.

There are many dental clinics, polyclinics and private practices in Beylikdüzü and the neighbouring districts of Esenyurt, Büyükçekmece and Avcılar. With so much choice, it helps to have concrete criteria to compare them. The sections below summarise them.

sections.h: What should happen at the first examination?
sections.html:
A good first examination isn't limited to the tooth that hurts. The whole mouth, the gums, your bite and any existing fillings or crowns are assessed, with a panoramic X-ray or 3D CT scan if needed.

  • Findings explained: You should be shown what the X-ray shows, in plain language.
  • Options presented: Most problems have more than one solution (e.g. implant, bridge or removable denture). The pros and cons of each should be discussed.
  • No pressure: You should be given time to think, not pushed into starting major treatment on the same day.
  • Room for questions: The time a dentist gives your questions says a lot about communication during treatment.

sections.h: Why a written treatment plan and price matter
sections.html:
Verbal quotes often change as extra items are added during treatment. A written plan makes clear from the start what will be done to each tooth, how many visits it will take and what each item costs.

What the plan should includeWhy it matters
Procedures, tooth by toothYou know exactly what you're paying for
Materials and brandsE.g. implant brand, zirconia or e.max
Possible additional proceduresBone grafts, sinus lifts or root canals don't come as a surprise

Check-ups and follow-upThe scope of aftercare is clear

At Dent32 we share the findings, options and an approximate cost in writing after the examination. We explain what shapes the cost in our article on dental implant cost factors.

sections.h: The dental team and their areas of focus
sections.html:
You're entitled to know in advance which dentist will carry out which treatment. Orthodontics, implant surgery, aesthetic dentistry and children's dentistry each call for different experience. When several disciplines plan together under one roof, cases that need, say, orthodontics followed by crowns run more smoothly.

We introduce our team and how we work on our about page. You can also see previous cases in our before-and-after gallery.

sections.h: How can you tell sterilisation is taken seriously?
sections.html:
• Instruments opened from sterile pouches for every patient
  • Single-use items (needles, gloves, suction tips) changed for every patient
  • Surfaces of the dental unit disinfected between patients
  • A dedicated sterilisation area in the clinic

Don't hesitate to ask about these; a careful clinic will be happy to answer.

sections.h: Access, opening days and urgent problems
sections.html:
Implant or orthodontic treatment involves several appointments over months. Easy access to the clinic and appointments outside your working hours make it easier to stay on schedule.

Dent32 is in Barış Mahallesi, Beylikdüzü, on the E-5 service road at Ginza Lavinya, and is open seven days a week. For toothache that starts in the evening or at the weekend, see our emergency toothache guide.

In short

A thorough examination, a written plan and cost, clarity about who treats you, visible hygiene standards and proper aftercare are the five things to look for when choosing a dental clinic in Beylikdüzü or anywhere in Istanbul.

faq.q: Is there a difference between a dental clinic and a dental polyclinic?
faq.a: In Türkiye, an oral and dental health polyclinic is a licensed facility where several dentists work together and specific requirements are met; a private practice usually has one dentist. In everyday language "dental clinic" is used for both. For patients, what matters most is the dentist's experience, planning and hygiene.

faq.q: Do I have to start treatment at the first visit?
faq.a: No. The first visit is for understanding your situation and discussing options. It's perfectly normal to take the plan home, think it over, or get a second opinion.

faq.q: Can I get a price over the phone or on WhatsApp?

title: Dental implants in Beylikdüzü, Istanbul: from examination to final tooth
desc: How dental implant treatment works at a clinic in Beylikdüzü, Istanbul: examination and CT scan, implant surgery, healing time, the final crown and check-ups, step by step.
seoTitle: Dental implants in Beylikdüzü, Istanbul | Dent32
seoDesc: How implant treatment works in Beylikdüzü: examination and CT scan, surgery, healing time, the final crown and check-ups, step by step.
lead: Dental implant treatment follows five basic steps: examination and CT scan, planning, placing the implant, waiting for it to fuse with the bone, and fitting the final tooth. For a single tooth, the process takes 3 to 6 months for most patients.

sections.html:
Implant planning starts with measuring the bone. A panoramic X-ray gives an overview, but the width and height of the bone and its distance from the nerve canal and sinus can only be measured reliably with a 3D cone-beam CT scan.

Gum health, neighbouring teeth, your bite and your general health (medication, diabetes, smoking) are assessed at the same time. Any decay or gum inflammation is treated before the implant.

sections.h: 2. Planning: how many implants, which brand, what kind of tooth?
sections.html:
The implant's diameter, length and angle are planned from the CT data. A single missing tooth is usually replaced with one implant and a crown; several missing teeth with implant-supported bridges; a whole arch with solutions such as All-on-Four.

SituationCommon solution
One missing toothOne implant + zirconia or porcelain crown
Two or three adjacent missing teethBridge on two implants
No teeth in the jawFixed bridge on 4–6 implants or an implant-retained denture
Insufficient boneImplant after bone graft or sinus lift

For full-arch options, see our All-on-Four guide and our article on implant-supported dentures.

The procedure is done under local anaesthetic. The gum is opened, a site is prepared in the bone and the implant is placed; the area is then stitched or a healing cap is fitted. A single implant usually takes 30–60 minutes.

Most patients feel pressure rather than pain. Mild swelling and tenderness for a few days are normal. We explain what to do afterwards in our implant aftercare guide.

The implant takes about 2–3 months to fuse in the lower jaw and 3–6 months in the upper jaw. A temporary tooth can be worn in visible areas during this time, so you're not left with a gap.

In some suitable cases the implant can be placed in the same visit as the extraction (immediate implant), with a temporary tooth on the same day. We cover when this is possible in how long implant treatment takes.

Once the implant has fused, an impression is taken (digital scan or conventional) and the final tooth is made. After a try-in, the crown or bridge is fixed to the implant. A few check-ups follow in the first year, then an examination and professional clean every six months.

How many visits?

For a single implant, 4–6 visits are enough for most patients: examination and CT, implant surgery, stitch check, impression, try-in, and fitting the final tooth.

sections.h: Questions to ask before getting an implant
sections.html:
• Which implant brand will be used, and will spare parts still be available years from now?
  • Is there enough bone, or will a graft or sinus lift be needed?
  • What material will the tooth on top be made of?
  • Will I have a temporary tooth while the implant heals?
  • What will the follow-up schedule be?

At Dent32 we plan implant treatment with an examination and CT scan and give you the plan in writing. See our implant treatment section or book an appointment. If you're travelling from abroad, our planning guide explains how to organise visits.

faq.q: How long does implant treatment take in Istanbul?
faq.a: With healthy, sufficient bone, a single implant is usually completed in 3–4 months. If a bone graft or sinus lift is needed, it can take 6–9 months overall.

faq.q: Am I put to sleep for implant surgery?
faq.a: Most implants are placed under local anaesthetic without sedation. If many implants are planned or you're very anxious, sedation options can be discussed.

faq.q: Can I go back to work after an implant?
faq.a: After a single implant most patients return to normal activities the next day. After more extensive surgery a few days' rest may be advised.

faq.q: Can I have implants if I've lost bone?
faq.a: In most cases, yes. If bone volume is insufficient, a bone graft or sinus lift can prepare the site; in some cases short or angled implants avoid the need for extra surgery.

title: What affects the cost of dental implants?
desc: What determines the price of a dental implant: implant brand, the crown on top, bone grafts and sinus lifts, number of implants and planning. What to check when comparing quotes.
seoDesc: What determines the price of a dental implant: brand, the crown, bone grafts and sinus lifts, number of implants and planning. Comparing quotes.
lead: The cost of a dental implant isn't a single number: the implant brand, the material of the tooth on top, additional procedures such as a bone graft or sinus lift, and the total number of implants together determine the price.

sections.h: Why can't everyone be quoted the same price?
sections.html:
Asking "how much is an implant?" is a bit like asking "how much is a car?": without knowing the model, the specification and the extras, a single answer would be misleading. Two patients may both need "one implant", but one needs only the implant and crown while the other also needs an extraction, a bone graft and a temporary tooth.

Single prices quoted over the phone or online often cover only the screw; the crown and extra procedures are added later. When comparing, look at a written plan for the whole treatment.

sections.h: The main factors that set the price
sections.html:
FactorEffect on cost
Implant brand and systemSystems with strong long-term clinical data and good parts availability usually cost more
The crown on topZirconia, porcelain or e.max, plus the type of abutment (connecting part)
Additional surgeryExtraction, bone graft, membrane, sinus lift
Number of implantsSingle tooth, bridge or full-arch plan
Temporary toothWearing a temporary tooth in visible areas while healing
Imaging and planningCT scan, and where needed digital planning and a surgical guide

sections.h: Does the implant brand really matter?
sections.html:
Yes, but not simply because "expensive is better". What matters is that the brand is backed by research, that spare parts will still be available years later when a crown needs replacing, and that the dentist is experienced with that system.

With an unknown or discontinued system, finding compatible parts later can be difficult. That's why the implant brand should be stated in your treatment plan.

sections.h: How do bone grafts and sinus lifts affect the cost?
sections.html:
If a tooth was lost long ago, the bone shrinks over time. Without enough bone, a graft or, in the upper back jaw, a sinus lift may be needed before or during implant placement. These add to both cost and overall time. See our article on bone grafts and sinus lifts for details.

Tip

If you have a tooth that needs to come out, discuss the implant plan at the extraction appointment. In some cases the implant can be placed at the same visit, or steps can be taken to limit bone loss.

sections.h: What to watch out for with very low prices
sections.html:
• Ask whether the price covers only the screw or also the abutment and crown.
  • Ask for the implant brand and crown material in writing.
  • Be wary of a final plan made without a CT scan.
  • Ask how check-ups and any complications will be handled.

An implant is meant to stay in your mouth for many years. A small saving at the start can turn into a much larger cost if it needs to be redone.

sections.h: How is the price set at Dent32?
sections.html: After the examination and CT scan we share, item by item and in writing, what will be done to each tooth, the implant brand and crown material, and any additional procedures. If you send your X-rays and photos via WhatsApp we can give preliminary information. For the stages of treatment, see our step-by-step implant guide.

faq.q: Does the implant price include the crown?
faq.a: It depends on the clinic. Some prices cover only the implant screw, with the abutment and crown charged separately. Ask for these items to be listed separately in any quote.

faq.q: Why are implants in Türkiye often less expensive?
faq.a: Lower operating and laboratory costs are the main reasons. Quality depends on the clinic, the materials and the dentist, not the country, so compare written plans rather than headline prices.

faq.q: Can I pay in stages?
faq.a: We discuss payment options based on the plan after the examination. Because treatment spans months, payments can usually follow the treatment stages.

faq.q: Is a single implant or a bridge more economical?
faq.a: A bridge can look cheaper in the short term, but it requires reducing the neighbouring teeth and may need replacing later. See our implant or bridge article for a comparison.

title: Types of dental crowns: zirconia, e.max, porcelain and veneers compared
desc: What a dental crown is and when it's needed. The differences between zirconia, e.max (glass ceramic), porcelain-fused-to-metal and laminate veneers, how long they last and how to choose.
seoTitle: Types of dental crowns: zirconia, e.max and veneers | Dent32
seoDesc: When is a dental crown needed? Zirconia, e.max, porcelain-fused-to-metal and laminate veneers compared: lifespan and how to choose.
lead: A dental crown is a restoration that fully covers and protects a worn, broken, discoloured or root-filled tooth. The most common options are zirconia, e.max glass ceramic and porcelain fused to metal; a laminate veneer covers only the front surface and removes less tooth structure.

sections.html:
• Teeth weakened by large fillings
  • Broken or cracked teeth
  • After root canal treatment, especially back teeth
  • Severe discolouration that whitening can't lift
  • Teeth supporting a bridge, and teeth on implants
  • Comprehensive correction of shape and size

TypeAestheticsStrengthTypical use
ZirconiaNatural-looking, metal-freeVery highFront and back teeth, bridges, on implants
E.max (lithium disilicate)Very high translucencyHighFront teeth, single crowns, veneers
Porcelain fused to metalGood, but more opaqueHigh, long clinical track recordBack teeth, long bridges
Laminate veneerVery highHigh in the right caseFront surface of front teeth

We compare zirconia and porcelain in zirconia or porcelain, explain e.max in what are e.max crowns, and cover veneers in our laminate veneer guide.

sections.h: Which crown is right for you?
sections.html:
The choice depends on how much healthy tooth remains, where the tooth is, your bite force, whether you grind your teeth, your gum level and your aesthetic goals. Translucency matters most at the front; fracture resistance matters most at the back.

If a tooth is healthy and only its colour or shape needs changing, more conservative options such as veneers or bonding should be considered first. Unnecessary full crowns sacrifice healthy tooth structure.

Important

Crowns shouldn't be the first choice for "whiter teeth". If colour is the only issue, teeth whitening is considered first.

StageWhat happens
Examination and planningX-rays, smile design if needed, shade selection
Tooth preparationUnder local anaesthetic, the tooth is reduced by the thickness of the crown
ImpressionDigital scan or conventional impression; temporary crowns fitted
Try-inFit, shade and shape checked
CementationThe final crown is bonded and the bite checked

In most cases treatment is completed within 1–2 weeks. The number of visits depends on how many teeth are treated and whether other treatment is needed.

Well-planned, well-maintained crowns last ten years or more for most patients. The biggest threats are decay at the margins, gum disease and grinding. For sensitivity and care after crowns, see our aftercare guide. You can read about crown options at our Beylikdüzü clinic in the treatments section.

faq.q: How much is the tooth reduced for a crown?
faq.a: It depends on the material, typically around 1–2 mm. For a veneer, only 0.3–0.7 mm is removed from the front surface, sometimes none.

faq.q: Can a crowned tooth decay?
faq.a: The crown itself can't decay, but the tooth underneath can, especially at the gum line. That's why flossing and regular check-ups matter.

faq.q: Can crowns be whitened?
faq.a: No. Crowns, fillings and veneers don't change colour with whitening. If you're considering whitening, do it before your crowns are made.

faq.q: Does a root-filled tooth need a crown?
faq.a: Back teeth are more prone to fracture after root canal treatment, so a crown is often recommended. Front teeth and teeth with little tissue loss may only need a filling.

title: Root canal treatment: when is it needed, how many visits, does it hurt?
desc: What root canal treatment is, the symptoms that call for it, how many visits it takes and whether it hurts. Pain afterwards, whether a crown is needed, and why saving the tooth matters.
seoTitle: Root canal treatment: when, how many visits, does it hurt? | Dent32
seoDesc: When is root canal treatment needed, how many visits does it take and does it hurt? Pain afterwards, crowns and why saving the tooth matters.
lead: Root canal treatment cleans out a nerve (pulp) inflamed by decay or trauma, disinfects the canals and seals them. It's done under local anaesthetic, usually takes 1–2 visits, and aims to keep the tooth rather than extract it.

sections.h: Symptoms that may mean you need a root canal
sections.html:
• Pain after hot or cold that lingers
  • Spontaneous, throbbing pain that wakes you at night
  • Tenderness when biting or touching the tooth
  • Swelling of the gum or a pimple-like bump that discharges
  • Darkening of the tooth (especially after an injury)

Sometimes a nerve dies without any symptoms and is found on a routine X-ray, which is why regular check-ups matter.

sections.h: How is root canal treatment done?
sections.html:
1. X-rays show the number and length of roots and the extent of infection.
  2. Local anaesthetic is given and the tooth is isolated.
  3. Decay is removed and the nerve tissue is reached.
  4. The canals are cleaned and shaped with special instruments and rinsed with disinfecting solutions.
  5. The canals are filled with a sealing material.
  6. The tooth is restored with a permanent filling or crown.

sections.h: How many visits does it take?
sections.html:
SituationTypical visits
Vital but inflamed nerveUsually one
Dead nerve with infection at the root (abscess)Usually two, with medication placed in between
Redoing a previous root canalTwo or more

A visit usually lasts 45–90 minutes. Front teeth have fewer canals and take less time; molars take longer.

It's done under local anaesthetic and most patients feel no significant pain during treatment. In fact, it relieves the pain caused by the inflammation. Mild tenderness when biting for a few days afterwards is common and usually settles with simple painkillers.

When to call

If swelling increases, if pain gets worse rather than better over a few days, or if you develop a fever, contact the clinic.

sections.h: Do I need a crown after a root canal?
sections.html: Root-filled teeth, especially back teeth, are more prone to fracture because of lost tooth structure, so a crown is often recommended for molars. Front teeth or teeth with little tissue loss may only need a filling. See types of dental crowns.

Extraction can look quicker in the short term, but the missing tooth then needs replacing with an implant or bridge, which takes longer and costs more. Keeping the natural tooth is usually the first choice when possible. If a tooth has been lost, see implant or bridge. You can also read more in our treatments section.

faq.q: Can a root canal be done in one visit?
faq.a: If the nerve is still vital and there's no infection at the root, often yes. With an abscess, it's usually completed in two visits.

faq.q: How long does pain last after a root canal?
faq.a: Mild tenderness usually fades over 2–5 days. Increasing pain or swelling should be checked.

faq.q: How long does a root-filled tooth last?
faq.a: A well-treated and properly restored root-filled tooth can last many years, often for life.

faq.q: Can I have a root canal while pregnant?
faq.a: Yes, when needed; the second trimester is usually the most comfortable time. X-rays and medication are planned with your pregnancy in mind.

title: Implant or bridge? Which is better for a missing tooth?
desc: Implant or bridge for a missing tooth? A comparison of the effect on neighbouring teeth, bone loss, treatment time, cleaning, lifespan and cost.
lead: There are two fixed ways to replace a missing tooth: an implant placed in the jawbone, or a bridge supported by the neighbouring teeth. An implant leaves the neighbouring teeth untouched and helps preserve bone; a bridge is quicker but may require reducing healthy teeth.

sections.h: The key differences between an implant and a bridge
sections.html:
FeatureImplantBridge
Neighbouring teethUntouchedSupporting teeth are reduced
BoneTransfers chewing load to bone, slowing shrinkageBone under the gap continues to shrink
TimeUsually 3–6 monthsUsually 1–2 weeks
SurgeryMinor surgery neededNo surgery
CleaningBrush and floss like a natural toothSpecial floss or interdental brush under the bridge
Initial costUsually higherUsually lower

sections.h: When does an implant make more sense?
sections.html:
• When the teeth either side of the gap are healthy and unfilled: there's no reason to reduce them for a bridge.
  • When there's enough bone, or bone can be built up with a graft.
  • When you want a long-term, independent solution: if a problem ever arises with an implant, the neighbouring teeth aren't affected.
  • When several teeth in a row are missing and there aren't enough supporting teeth for a bridge.

For the stages and timeline, see how long implant treatment takes.

sections.h: When might a bridge be the better choice?
sections.html:
• When the neighbouring teeth already have large fillings or need crowns anyway: the bridge protects them at the same time.
  • When general health doesn't allow surgery.
  • When bone is very limited and the patient doesn't want extra surgery.
  • When treatment needs to be completed quickly.

Our article on types of dental crowns explains the materials used for bridges.

Both can last many years when well planned and properly cared for. With bridges, the most common problems are decay starting at the crown margins of the supporting teeth and gum problems, so cleaning under the bridge is essential. With implants, the main risk is inflammation of the gum and bone around the implant (peri-implantitis).

Over the long term implants usually have the edge, because even if the crown is replaced the implant itself can stay in place.

Important

Leaving a gap for a long time can let the opposing tooth over-erupt into the space and the neighbouring teeth tip into it. Whichever option you choose, it's best not to wait too long.

The decision depends on the neighbouring teeth, bone volume, general health, budget and expectations. At the examination we explain both options with their pros and cons and compare them in writing. Get in touch to book an appointment.

faq.q: Can I switch from a bridge to an implant later?
faq.a: Yes. The bridge can be removed and an implant placed in the gap; but because the supporting teeth were reduced, they will need crowns too. Bone is assessed separately.

faq.q: Which is recommended for a single missing tooth?
faq.a: If the teeth on either side are healthy, an implant is usually recommended because no healthy tooth structure is removed. If the neighbouring teeth need crowns anyway, a bridge can also be suitable.

faq.q: What is an implant bridge?
faq.a: When several teeth are missing, a bridge is made on two or more implants instead of placing one implant per tooth. Natural teeth aren't touched.

faq.q: Is a removable denture also an option?
faq.a: Yes. Partial dentures cost less but offer less comfort and chewing efficiency than fixed solutions.

title: Toothache at night or at the weekend: what to do and when it's urgent
desc: What you can do at home for toothache that starts in the evening or at the weekend, which situations are urgent, broken teeth, lost crowns, facial swelling and a dentist open at weekends in Beylikdüzü, Istanbul.
seoTitle: Toothache at night or at the weekend | Dent32
seoDesc: Toothache in the evening or at the weekend: what to do at home, what's urgent, broken teeth, lost crowns, facial swelling and weekend care.
lead: When toothache starts, first judge how severe it is and whether there's swelling or fever. Swelling spreading to the face or neck, difficulty swallowing or breathing, and a high temperature are emergencies; otherwise, painkillers and cold compresses can bring relief until you're seen.

sections.html:
SituationWhat to do
Swelling spreading to the face, under the eye or neck, with feverSee a dentist the same day; if swallowing or breathing is difficult, go to hospital A&E immediately
A permanent tooth knocked outHold it by the crown, not the root, keep it in milk and see a dentist as soon as possible (ideally within an hour)
Bleeding that won't stop (after extraction)Press with gauze for 30 minutes; if it continues, call the clinic or go to A&E
Throbbing pain that keeps you awakePainkiller and the earliest available appointment
Broken tooth, lost filling or crownIf there's no pain, an appointment within a few days

sections.h: What can you do at home until you're seen?
sections.html:
• Take a painkiller you've used before and that suits you, at the dose on the leaflet.
  • If there's swelling, apply cold to the outside of the cheek; don't apply heat.
  • If food is stuck between teeth, remove it gently with floss.
  • Rinse gently with warm salt water.
  • Avoid chewing on that side and avoid very hot, cold or sugary foods.
What not to do

Don't place painkiller tablets on the tooth or gum; they burn the tissue. Don't take antibiotics without a prescription; unless the source of infection is treated, the problem comes back.

SymptomPossible cause
Brief twinge with coldSensitivity, exposed root or small cavity
Lingering pain made worse by heatNerve inflammation; root canal treatment may be needed
Pain on bitingInfection at the root, cracked tooth or high filling
Pain at the back with limited mouth openingInflammation around a wisdom tooth
Gum swelling with dischargeAbscess

Nerve inflammation and abscesses often need root canal treatment; for pain from wisdom teeth, see our wisdom tooth guide.

sections.h: Broken tooth or lost crown: what to do
sections.html:
If you can find the broken piece, keep it in a clean container; on front teeth it can sometimes be bonded back. If a sharp edge irritates your tongue or cheek, cover it with sugar-free gum or orthodontic wax.

Don't glue a lost crown back yourself. Keep it and call the clinic. For other crown problems, see our guide to care after crowns.

sections.h: A dentist open at weekends in Beylikdüzü
sections.html:
Dent32 sees patients seven days a week at its clinic on the E-5 service road in Beylikdüzü. For toothache that starts in the evening or at the weekend, message us on WhatsApp for the earliest available time. Sending a photo and describing your symptoms helps us prioritise. Find our contact details here.

If facial swelling is growing quickly or you have difficulty swallowing or breathing, go straight to the nearest hospital emergency department.

faq.q: Does toothache go away on its own?
faq.a: The pain can ease temporarily, but that doesn't mean the problem is solved. A dying nerve can stop hurting while infection continues at the root. Even if the pain goes, get it checked.

faq.q: Are antibiotics enough for a dental abscess?
faq.a: Antibiotics can help control spreading infection but don't remove the cause. A lasting solution needs root canal treatment or extraction.

faq.q: Which painkiller should I take for toothache at night?
faq.a: You can take a painkiller you've used before and that suits you, at the dose on the leaflet. If you have a chronic condition, are pregnant or take regular medication, ask a pharmacist.

faq.q: Can I get a weekend appointment?
faq.a: Yes. Our clinic is open seven days a week; message us on WhatsApp for an available time.

title: What are e.max crowns? How they differ from zirconia and who they suit
desc: What e.max (lithium disilicate glass ceramic) crowns are and how they compare with zirconia: aesthetics, strength, uses, lifespan and when they're the right choice.
seoTitle: What are e.max crowns? How they differ from zirconia | Dent32
seoDesc: What e.max (lithium disilicate) crowns are and how they compare with zirconia: aesthetics, strength, uses, lifespan and when to choose them.
lead: E.max is a highly translucent crown material made from a glass ceramic called lithium disilicate. It stands out for its natural look on front teeth; because it's slightly less strong than zirconia, it's chosen with care for back teeth and for people who grind.

sections.html:
E.max is a glass ceramic system for metal-free, all-ceramic restorations. It transmits and reflects light very much like natural enamel, so it blends well with neighbouring natural teeth, especially at the front.

It can be made as crowns, laminate veneers, inlays and onlays. Because it's bonded to the tooth surface (adhesive cementation), it can be made thin, allowing less tooth structure to be removed.

FeatureE.maxZirconia
TranslucencyVery highHigh (improved in newer zirconias)
Fracture resistanceHighVery high
Minimum thicknessCan be made thinUsually needs a little more thickness
BridgesLimited to short front bridgesSuitable for long bridges and implants
Typical useFront teeth, veneers, single crownsBack teeth, bridges, on implants

For zirconia versus porcelain fused to metal, see zirconia or porcelain.

• People with colour, shape or small chip problems on front teeth
  • Smile design cases where a natural look is the top priority
  • Situations where minimal tooth removal is wanted (veneers, inlays and onlays)

For people who grind at night, or in back teeth with heavy chewing forces, zirconia is usually the safer choice. If you grind, a night guard is recommended whatever the material.

Used in the right case and well bonded, e.max restorations last for many years. The key factors are case selection, controlling grinding and oral hygiene. See our guide to sensitivity and care after crowns.

In short

For the most natural look on front teeth, e.max; for back teeth, bridges or grinders, zirconia is usually more suitable. The decision is made at the examination and as part of the smile plan.
Smile design cases often combine both: e.max at the front and zirconia at the back, balancing aesthetics and strength. See our smile design guide, or compare all options in types of dental crowns.

faq.q: E.max or veneers?
faq.a: A veneer is a type of restoration; e.max is a material. Veneers are often made from e.max glass ceramic. How much of the tooth is covered (front only or all of it) depends on the tooth's condition.

faq.q: Can e.max break?
faq.a: Fractures are rare when the case is right and the thickness is adequate. Grinding, biting hard objects (pens, seeds, ice) and insufficient thickness raise the risk.

faq.q: Does e.max stain?
faq.a: No. The glass ceramic surface resists staining from tea, coffee and smoking. Any staining at the edges can usually be polished away.

faq.q: Can e.max be used on back teeth?
faq.a: It can be used for single crowns on back teeth, but with heavy bite forces or grinding, zirconia is usually safer.

title: After dental implant surgery: eating, drinking, smoking and care
desc: What to do after implant surgery: the first 24 hours, swelling and pain, what to eat and when, smoking, exercise, brushing and long-term implant care.
seoTitle: After dental implant surgery: eating, smoking, care | Dent32
lead: In the first 24 hours after implant surgery, cold compresses, soft lukewarm food, leaving the area alone and not smoking all help healing. Over the long term, regular cleaning and check-ups are what most determine how long an implant lasts.

sections.html:
• Gauze: Bite on the gauze provided for 30–45 minutes.
  • Cold compress: Apply ice to the outside of the cheek for 15–20 minutes at a time.
  • Eating: Don't eat until the numbness wears off; then choose soft, lukewarm food.
  • Rinsing: Avoid vigorous rinsing and spitting on the first day so the clot isn't disturbed.
  • Straws: Don't use them; the suction can increase bleeding.
  • Medication: Take the prescribed painkillers and, if given, antibiotics as directed.

sections.h: What can I eat, and when?
sections.html:
PeriodRecommendedAvoid
First 2–3 daysYoghurt, lukewarm soup, mash, puddings, soft omeletteHot drinks, hard or spicy food, alcohol
First 1–2 weeksPasta, rice, cooked vegetables, fish, meatballsNuts, crusty bread, seeds
While the implant healsNormal diet, chewing on the other sidePutting heavy load directly on the implant

sections.h: Are swelling, bruising and pain normal?
sections.html:
Yes. Swelling usually peaks on day 2 or 3 and then subsides. Mild bruising on the cheek can appear, especially after several implants or a bone graft, and fades within a week. Pain is usually controlled with simple painkillers.

When to call the clinic

If bleeding doesn't stop despite gauze, swelling and pain increase after day 3, you have a rising temperature, a bad taste or discharge, or numbness hasn't worn off by the next day.

sections.h: Can I smoke after an implant?
sections.html: Smoking reduces blood flow in the gum and bone, slows healing and significantly increases the risk of the implant failing to fuse. Avoid smoking completely for at least the first 48–72 hours, and ideally throughout the healing period. We cover how smoking and diabetes affect implants in who can get dental implants.

On the day of surgery you can gently brush the teeth away from the surgical site. From the next day, clean the surgical area carefully with a soft brush. If advised, use lukewarm salt water or an antiseptic mouthwash.

Stitches are usually removed after 7–10 days or dissolve on their own.

sections.h: Long term: how to look after an implant
sections.html:
• Brush twice a day and use an interdental brush or floss around the implant
  • A check-up and professional clean every six months
  • A night guard if you grind or clench
  • Prompt check-up if you notice bleeding gums

Implants can't decay, but the gum and bone around them can become inflamed (peri-implantitis). Caught early, it's much easier to treat. See our articles on bleeding gums and night guards.

faq.q: When can I exercise after an implant?
faq.a: Avoid strenuous exercise for the first 3–5 days, as raised blood pressure can increase bleeding. Light walking is fine from the next day.

faq.q: Can I drink coffee after an implant?
faq.a: Avoid hot drinks on the first day. From the following days, lukewarm coffee is fine.

faq.q: Are antibiotics always needed after an implant?
faq.a: Not for every patient. Whether antibiotics are needed depends on the extent of surgery and your health, and is decided by the dentist.

faq.q: How do I know if the implant has taken?
faq.a: During healing an implant usually gives no symptoms. It's checked clinically and with X-rays at follow-ups, and its stability is confirmed before the final tooth is fitted.

title: Bleeding and receding gums: causes and treatment
desc: Why gums bleed and recede. Signs of gingivitis and periodontitis, scaling, root planing, treatment for gum recession and home care.
lead: Gums that bleed when you brush are usually the first sign of gum inflammation caused by plaque and tartar. Caught early, it reverses completely with a professional clean and good home care; left untreated, it can progress to periodontitis, which affects the bone that holds the teeth.

sections.html:
Bacterial plaque building up on the teeth inflames the gums. Inflamed gums become red and swollen and bleed easily when brushing or flossing. When plaque hardens it becomes tartar, which a toothbrush can no longer remove.

  • Inadequate brushing and no flossing
  • Tartar
  • Smoking (which can mask bleeding and hide the disease)
  • Pregnancy and hormonal changes
  • Diabetes
  • Some medications, including blood thinners

Gingivitis (gum inflammation)Periodontitis (advanced gum disease)
Tissue affectedGums onlyGums and the bone holding the teeth
SignsRedness, swelling, bleedingRecession, bad breath, loose or spreading teeth
Reversible?Fully reversibleLost bone usually doesn't return; the disease is halted
TreatmentProfessional clean and home careDeep cleaning, root planing, surgery if needed

The most common causes of recession are periodontitis and brushing too hard. Grinding, thin gum tissue, orthodontic movement and tight lip or cheek attachments can contribute. Recession exposes the root surface, which can lead to sensitivity, root decay and cosmetic concerns.

Brushing

Use a soft-bristled brush and avoid a horizontal sawing motion. Angle the brush at 45 degrees to the gum and use small circular movements.

1. Examination, gum pocket measurements and X-rays to assess bone level
  2. Scaling and polishing
  3. Root planing under local anaesthetic if needed
  4. Re-assessment after 4–8 weeks
  5. Surgical procedures such as flap surgery or gum grafts in advanced cases
  6. Regular maintenance (usually every 3–6 months)

We answer common questions about scaling in our article on professional teeth cleaning.

sections.h: Why gum health affects other treatments
sections.html: The long-term success of implants, crowns and orthodontics depends on healthy gums. A similar inflammation (peri-implantitis) can develop around implants. That's why gum disease is treated first. Read more in our treatments section or book an appointment at our Beylikdüzü clinic.

faq.q: My gums bleed. Should I stop brushing?
faq.a: No. Bleeding is a sign of inflammation; gentle but regular brushing and flossing help it settle. If it doesn't improve in a week or two, see a dentist.

faq.q: Do receded gums grow back?
faq.a: Not on their own. In suitable cases, procedures such as gum grafts can cover the root again. The cause of the recession is addressed first.

faq.q: Can bad breath come from gum disease?
faq.a: Yes, gum disease and bacteria on the tongue are among the most common causes of persistent bad breath.

faq.q: Is bleeding gums normal in pregnancy?
faq.a: It's common because of hormonal changes (pregnancy gingivitis). A check-up and a clean are still recommended; scaling is safe during pregnancy.

title: Bone grafts and sinus lifts: can I have implants with too little bone?
desc: What bone grafts and sinus lifts are, when they're needed, whether they hurt and how much they extend implant treatment. Open versus closed sinus lift.
seoTitle: Bone grafts and sinus lifts: implants with little bone | Dent32
lead: If the jawbone isn't wide or tall enough to hold an implant, a bone graft is used to build it up; in the upper back jaw, the sinus floor can be raised (sinus lift) to make room. These procedures often make implants possible, but they lengthen treatment.

sections.html:
Once a tooth is lost, the bone that held it no longer receives chewing load and gradually becomes thinner and shorter. Most of this loss happens in the first months after extraction. Advanced gum disease, long-term use of removable dentures and trauma can also cause bone loss.

The upper back jaw has an extra issue: after teeth are lost, the sinus can expand downwards, reducing the bone height left for an implant.

A bone graft is a material that acts as scaffolding for new bone. It can be the patient's own bone, processed human or animal bone, or a synthetic material. It's usually covered with a membrane and is gradually replaced by the patient's own bone over a few months.

UseWhen?
Filling the extraction socket (socket preservation)At extraction, to limit bone loss if an implant is planned
Graft at the same time as the implantFor small bone defects
Graft first, implant laterWhen bone is very thin; the implant usually follows 4–6 months later

In a sinus lift, the membrane lining the floor of the sinus in the upper back jaw is gently raised and bone graft material is placed beneath it, creating the bone height needed for an implant.
